'''Willowbrook''' is a neighborhood in [[Staten Island]], one of the five boroughs of [[New York City]]. It is located in the region of the island usually referred to as [[Mid-Island, Staten Island|Mid-Island]], immediately to the south of [[Port Richmond, Staten Island|Port Richmond]], to the west of [[Meiers Corners, Staten Island|Meiers Corners]] and [[Westerleigh, Staten Island|Westerleigh]], to the north of [[New Springville, Staten Island|New Springville]], and to the east of [[Bulls Head, Staten Island|Bulls Head]].

==History==
Named for a brook that flowed through the area's farmland, Willowbrook once lay at the heart of the island's agricultural zone, and first saw other significant development when a [[military hospital]] opened there during [[World War II]]. After the war ended the property became the site of [[Willowbrook State School]], a state-run institution for [[intellectual disability|intellectually disabled]] children that became the scene of a national scandal in the 1970s when it was revealed that the children housed there were the victims of widespread abuse and neglect. The facility was forced to close by 1987, and six years later a campus of the [[College of Staten Island]] opened at the site.  [[Willowbrook Park]], a large city park, borders the college on the west.  It was also home to the [[Seaview Hospital]] [[tuberculosis]] [[sanatorium]], added to the [[National Register of Historic Places]] in 2005.<ref name="nris">{{NRISref|2009a}}</ref>

The neighborhood was also drastically transformed with the opening of the [[Verrazzano–Narrows Bridge]] in November 1964. Soon after this, the farms were sold and broken up, and residential housing was built on the property. Many of the owners of the newly built homes were Jewish families, and as a result, Willowbrook became the center of the island's Orthodox Jewish community, which from the turn of the 20th century until the late 1960s and early 1970s was primarily  centered in Staten Island's [[North Shore, Staten Island|North Shore]] neighborhood of [[Tompkinsville, Staten Island|Tompkinsville]] along with most of Staten Island's then-small Jewish population.

The 2010s saw a great influx to the Jewish community in Willowbrook, because of the housing crisis in [[Brooklyn]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/news/2016/08/25/priced-out-of-williamsburg--orthodox-jewish-community-eyes-staten-island-neighborhoods.html|title=Priced Out of Williamsburg, Orthodox Jewish Community Eyes Staten Island Neighborhoods|work=TWC News|access-date=2017-06-11|language=en}}</ref>

==Demographics==
{{Unreferenced section|date=October 2018}}
For census purposes, the New York City Department of City Planning classifies Willowbrook as part of a larger Neighborhood Tabulation Area called New Springville-Willowbrook-Bulls Head-Travis SI0204. This designated neighborhood had 42,871 inhabitants based on data from the [[2020 United States census|2020 United States Census]]. This was an increase of 3,561 persons (9.1%) from the 39,310 counted in [[2010 United States census|2010]]. The neighborhood had a population density of 8.5 inhabitants per acre (14,500/sq mi; 5,600/km<sup>2</sup>).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://popfactfinder.planning.nyc.gov/explorer/ntas/SI0303|title=Census Data for SI0303|date=2020|access-date=November 27, 2025|website=New York City Department of Planning|url-status=live}}</ref>

The racial makeup of the neighborhood was 59.5% (25,502) [[White Non-Hispanic|White (Non-Hispanic)]], 3.0% (1,295) [[Black Non-Hispanic|Black (Non-Hispanic)]], 19.6% (8,401) [[Asian (U.S. Census)|Asian]], and 2.6% (1,136) from two or more races. [[Hispanic (U.S. Census)|Hispanic]] or [[Latino (U.S. Census)|Latino]] of any race were 15.2% (6,537) of the population.<ref name=":0" />

According to the [[2020 United States census|2020 United States Census]], this area has many cultural communities of over 1,000 inhabitants. This include residents who identify as [[Mexican Americans|Mexican]], [[Stateside Puerto Ricans|Puerto Rican]], [[Albanian Americans|Albanian]], [[German Americans|German]], [[Irish Americans|Irish]], [[Italian Americans|Italian]], [[Polish Americans|Polish]], [[Russian Americans|Russian]], [[Egyptian Americans|Egyptian]], [[Korean Americans|Korean]], and [[Chinese Americans|Chinese]].<ref name=":0" />

71.0% of the households had at least one family present. Out of the 10,773 households, 51.0% had a married couple (20.7% with a child under 18), 4.4% had a cohabiting couple (1.4% with a child under 18), 16.8% had a single male (1.5% with a child under 18), and 27.9% had a single female (3.9% with a child under 18). 31.8% of households had children. In this neighborhood, 33.4% of non-vacant housing units are renter-occupied.<ref name=":0" />

== Religion ==
Young Israel of Staten Island — an [[Orthodox Judaism|Orthodox]] [[synagogue]] that is the island's largest Jewish house of worship — is located in Willowbrook, as are a number of smaller Orthodox congregations, including [[Hasidic]] and [[Sephardic]] congregations. Although Willowbrook is home to non-Orthodox Jews as well, there are no non-Orthodox synagogues in the community.

==Education==
===School===
Willowbrook is the location of P.S. 54, an [[elementary school]] administered by the [[New York City Department of Education]].

===Library===
The [[New York Public Library]] (NYPL)'s Todt Hill-Westerleigh branch is located at 2550 Victory Boulevard on the border between Willowbrook and Westerleigh. The three-story branch opened in 1991.<ref>{{cite web | title=About the Todt Hill-Westerleigh Library | website=The New York Public Library | date=April 18, 1991 | url=https://www.nypl.org/about/locations/todt-hill-westerleigh | access-date=March 19, 2019}}</ref>

==Transportation==
